citation.source: USDA FoodData Central (fdc.nal.usda.gov), raw potato, flesh and skin
citation.note: Figures are in the range USDA FoodData Central publishes for raw potato — this repo has not looked up the exact current FDC entry/ID to confirm the precise values, and potato composition genuinely varies by cultivar (see garlic.json's cultivar note for the same caveat on a different crop).

citation.source: Idaho Potato Commission, "Storing Idaho Potatoes in the Refrigerator...Right or Wrong?" (Dr. Potato column) — via convergent secondary corroboration; the primary idahopotato.com page returned HTTP 403 to direct fetch this session
citation.note: A cool (45-55F/7-13C), dark, well-ventilated pantry — NOT the refrigerator — for roughly 1.5-2 months (a cool basement at the low end of that range can extend to 2-4 months; the figure here is the more commonly-cited plain-pantry range). doNotRefrigerate is the real, cited, food-QUALITY (not food-safety) reason: below ~42F/6C, potato starch converts to sugar, causing excess browning and higher acrylamide formation when later fried (crispy-french-fries.json/fry.json's own oilTempC-driven crisping is the exact downstream process this would visibly affect) — directly connects to this repo's own existing frying-physics citations rather than an isolated fact.

citation.source: Choi & Okos (1986), "Effects of Temperature and Composition on the Thermal Properties of Foods" — the standard predictive model in food engineering for deriving thermal conductivity/density/specific heat from a food's composition
citation.note: densityKgPerM3/thermalConductivityWPerMK: this repo has not run potato's actual composition through the Choi-Okos model to re-derive these two — recalled as being in the right range for a starchy tuber, not computed. specificHeatJPerKgK, added 2026-08-15, IS actually computed from it (a real upgrade in rigor for this one field, not a rename): Choi-Okos's published component equation for carbohydrate (cp = 1.5488 + 1.9625e-3*t - 5.9399e-6*t^2 kJ/(kg*K), t in Celsius) evaluated at a 50C reference gives ~1632 J/(kg*K); combined with water.json's own already-cited 4186 J/(kg*K) for the water component, mass-weighted by this file's own composition.nutrientsPer100g (water_g=79, carbohydrate_g=17, normalized over the tracked 96% since protein/fiber/ash aren't tracked here) gives 3733.74 J/(kg*K), rounded to 3730. Real, named limitation: the untracked ~4% (protein/fiber/ash) means this is a two-component approximation of the full six-component Choi-Okos model, not the complete calculation. Used by src/heat-penetration.ts's thermalDiffusivityM2PerS.

citation.source: America's Test Kitchen, "Boiling Potatoes" (americastestkitchen.com/how_tos/5964-boiling-potatoes) — the same size-banded figure (2-2.5 inch diameter) already cited in src/potato-doneness.ts's 'whole' entry, promoted here to a real structured field 2026-08-15 instead of living only as prose.
citation.note: A professional test-kitchen source, not independently re-verified against a primary/regulatory source. Same figure potato-doneness.ts's own 'whole' entry already used — this field is the single source of truth for it now; that file's description/doc comment point here rather than repeating the number independently.

metadata.notes: possibleStates/capabilities originally grounded in CLAUDE_DEV_CTX.md's own potato examples, including its illustrative INVALID_TRANSITIONS map (boiled/fried/mashed) and its 'cannot peel a potato that is already boiled' line — CORRECTED 2026-08-15, on direct user correction: that specific claim is factually wrong (boil-in-jacket-then-peel is a real, common potato-salad technique), so it was never actually enforced against it; see invalidTransitionsNote below for what this field's real, checked content is instead. statePrerequisites.cut originally required 'peeled' unconditionally; widened 2026-08-13 to ['washed','peeled'] (see ingredient.ts's array-valued statePrerequisites) so skin-on cuts (rustic wedges, skin-on fries — a real, legitimate style, not an oversight) are representable too, not just the peeled path. boil/fry/bake are three distinct verbs on purpose: cooked in water vs. oil vs. dry heat give different results, so they're not collapsed into one generic COOK verb. mash was NOT wired up for a long time (no 'mash' action existed despite 'mashed' being a listed state) — closed 2026-08-13, see mashNote below. possibleTags/salt: seasoning is orthogonal to possibleStates — a 'salted boiled potato' is state 'boiled' plus tag 'salted' held at once, not a single combined state.
metadata.mashNote: MASH (data/actions/mash.json) + isMashable, closed 2026-08-13 — the single most glaring gap found while auditing this repo's own honesty: 'mashed' had been a listed possibleState since the first potato entity existed, with ZERO action ever producing it, the exact same shape of dead-label gap 'heat as a place' work found in pan.json's unreachable 'hot'/'cold' states. statePrerequisites.mash: ['boiled','baked'] — you cannot mash a raw potato; it must already be cooked soft via one of two real, distinct paths (conventional boiled-then-mashed, or baked-then-scooped for twice-baked). Once mashed, FRY still works on it with ZERO further changes (FRY has no statePrerequisites entry at all) — a mashed potato can be pan-fried directly (a real, simple 'potato cake'/leftover-mash technique), though a true breaded croquette (mash -> shape -> bread/batter -> fry) still can't be fully represented: no coating/breading mechanism exists in this vocabulary (named, not built — same discipline as every other scoped-out gap here).
metadata.gratedNote: GRATE (data/actions/grate.json) + isGratable, added 2026-08-13, for hash browns/rösti — deliberately its OWN verb/tool (grater.json), not a sixth value on CUT's shape enum: a box grater shreds by friction against a grating surface, physically nothing like a knife's slicing motion, and folding it into CUT would have wrongly implied a knife produces grated potato. statePrerequisites.grate: ['washed','peeled'], same either-path reasoning as cut's own prerequisite (skin-on grating for rustic hash browns is a real, legitimate style too). Whether the grated shreds are rinsed/squeezed of surface starch (crispier, more separate hash browns) or left as-is (starch helps bind a rösti into one cake) is a further real technique distinction this schema does not model — same depth limit as everywhere else in this vocabulary.
metadata.combineNote: isCombinableBase + statePrerequisites.combine: 'fried' — tortilla de patatas combines already-fried potato with beaten egg, not raw. See data/actions/combine.json and data/entities/tortilla_mixture.json (the first entity in this repo to actually use structure.composite/components).
metadata.restNote: isRestable + REST (data/actions/rest.json), added 2026-08-16, directly closes the gap par-fry.json's own restNote and crispy-french-fries.json's own restGapNote already named: the cited real ~10-minute rest between PAR_FRY and the finishing FRY had no way to be expressed in a RecipeScript before this verb existed. crispy-french-fries.json updated the same day to actually include it — see that recipe's own updated notes.
metadata.combinePotatoOnionNote: Added 2026-08-16, directly closing the 'tortilla de patatas CON cebolla' gap tortilla-de-patatas.json's own metadata named. statePrerequisites.combine_potato_onion: 'sliced' — a genuinely different prerequisite from statePrerequisites.combine's 'fried' above, because the real technique is different: potato and onion are combined RAW (both sliced) and fried TOGETHER afterward, not fried separately then merged. Reuses the SAME isCombinableBase capability this entity already asserts for the original combine — see data/actions/combine_potato_onion.json and data/entities/onion.json's combinePotatoOnionNote for the full two-stage chain.
metadata.washedTagNote: Changed 2026-08-15: 'washed' moved from possibleStates to possibleTags (and data/actions/wash.json's outputs from transformedState to addsTag). It was never actually a mutually-exclusive FORM the way 'peeled'/'sliced'/'fried' are — a potato is still, physically, washed after being peeled — but modeling it as a state meant WASH-then-PEEL silently lost that fact, since state holds exactly one value. statePrerequisites.cut/grate: ['washed','peeled'] did not need to change: engine.ts's check now matches each entry against either state OR tags, so both remain valid, order-independent predecessors, and washing both before AND after peeling (if a cook genuinely wants to) is now representable too, not just tolerated. Found and fixed the same day a user correctly pushed back on this repo's own real-world potato-prep order — see LEARNINGS.md 2026-08-15.
metadata.seasoningNote: pepper/chili added to allowedTransformations 2026-08-13 alongside salt, the first entity to use all three seasoning verbs (data/actions/pepper.json, chili.json) — same addsTag/possibleTags mechanism as salt, no recipe currently exercises them (built to make the vocabulary capable, not forced into an existing dish that wasn't asked to have pepper/chili). acid added 2026-08-15, same shape, same discipline — see data/actions/acid.json and vinegar.json.
metadata.simmerNote: SIMMER (data/actions/simmer.json) added 2026-08-13, isSimmerable alongside isBoilable — reaches the SAME 'boiled' state as BOIL, deliberately (see simmer.json's sharedTransformedStateNote), just via a gentler, lower-turbulence process real technique actually recommends for whole/halved potatoes to avoid broken skins and starch-clouded water. No recipe currently exercises it (same 'capable, not forced in' discipline as pepper/chili above).
metadata.boilDonenessNote: Added 2026-08-14, directly answering 'how long, depending on temperature and piece size' — src/potato-doneness.ts's POTATO_BOIL_DONENESS gives boil.json's/simmer.json's new pieceSize parameter a real, cited seconds range (whole/halved_or_quartered/diced), the potato sibling of src/egg-doneness.ts's EGG_BOIL_DONENESS. 'halved'/'quartered' were added to cut.json's shape enum in the same change specifically because this table needed a real CUT-produced state to correspond to its 'halved_or_quartered' category — neither existed before (only sliced/diced/julienne/chopped/minced did, none of which is what a real recipe means by 'quartered potatoes for boiling'). Heat-source/preheat-time dependence ('depending on the temperature') needed ZERO new code here — src/place.ts and src/heat-source.ts, built for the egg case, are already fully general over which ingredient is being boiled; see scripts/boil-potato-as-a-robot.ts for the proof.
metadata.storageLifeNote: storageLifeByState added 2026-08-17, ROADMAP.md's 'Storage/shelf-life common knowledge' gap (see ingredient.ts's StorageLifeSchema for the full reasoning, including why this is DECLARATION only). 'raw' only — every other state here (peeled/cut-shapes/boiled/fried/baked/mashed) is an intermediate or finished PREPARATION step within one recipe's own timeframe, not something this repo has a real, separately-cited storage figure for (the same 'a leftover cooked dish's own shelf life is a RecipeScript-level fact, not an Entity-level one' scoping egg.json's own identical note names). doNotRefrigerate is the one fact here that's genuinely counter-intuitive (most raw perishables DO want refrigeration) and directly ties back to this entity's own existing frying-physics citations (cut-dimensions.ts/heat-penetration.ts/fry.json's oilTempC) rather than being an isolated storage fact.
metadata.parFryNote: isParFryable + PAR_FRY (data/actions/par-fry.json), added 2026-08-13 in response to a direct question about how shape/size/oil temperature affect fried potato outcome. Unlike SIMMER, PAR_FRY deliberately does NOT reuse FRY's 'fried' transformedState — 'par_fried' is a genuinely different, unfinished intermediate (pale, soft, not crisp), not the same dish reached more gently, so collapsing it into 'fried' would have been the wrong call here even though it was the right call for SIMMER/BOIL (see simmer.json's sharedTransformedStateNote for why that distinction matters and isn't just inconsistency). No statePrerequisites entry added for 'fry' itself — FRY stays callable from any state, same as before, so a direct single-stage fry from 'peeled'/'raw' still works unchanged; PAR_FRY then FRY is an additional, not exclusive, path.
metadata.invalidTransitionsNote: Closed 2026-08-15, ROADMAP.md Phase 4's 'single largest unbuilt piece' — CORRECTED the same day, same session, on direct user correction. The FIRST version of this field forbade every processed state (sliced/diced/.../boiled/fried/baked) from reverting to 'peeled', following CLAUDE_DEV_CTX.md's own literal illustrative example ('cannot peel a potato that is already boiled', also in the top-level notes field above and in peel.json's own metadata since this repo's first commit) uncritically. That example is FACTUALLY WRONG: peeling a boiled potato is a real, common technique (boil-in-jacket, then peel while hot — the standard method for many potato salad recipes, and for jacket/new potatoes generally), not a physical impossibility. Corrected by removing every 'X forbids peeled' entry — this repo had never actually verified that claim against real technique before enforcing it, and enforcing it surfaced the error immediately (see LEARNINGS.md 2026-08-15). What survives is the one entry that IS structurally defensible: 'mashed' forbids reverting to any intact-piece state (peeled/cut-shapes/boiled/par_fried/baked) — once puréed, there is no discrete skin or shape left for PEEL/CUT/GRATE/BOIL/BAKE to act on, a genuine physical fact, not an assumed convention. Deliberately does NOT forbid 'mashed' -> 'fried' — mashed-into-a-potato-cake (fry.json has no statePrerequisites at all) is a real, celebrated technique (see mashNote above).
metadata.fryingScienceNote: The real physics behind 'depends on shape, size, oil temperature': Kalogianni & Smith, "Effect of frying variables on French fry properties," International Journal of Food Science and Technology 48(4):758-770 (2013) — https://doi.org/10.1111/ijfs.12024 — found water removal and oil uptake are NOT simply linked (a thicker crust from more water loss did not mean proportionally more oil absorbed), most property change happens in the first 1-2 minutes of frying, and crust thickness plateaus (~0.35-0.46mm) despite continued heat penetration, due to compensatory shrinkage. None of this is modeled numerically here — CUT's 'shape' parameter (data/actions/cut.json) already gives potato a real, distinct piece-size state, but nothing connects that state to FRY's/PAR_FRY's durationSeconds or oilTempC the way a real fryer (or a real cook) would adjust for it. Same informational-only depth limit as every other parameter in this vocabulary (see fry.json's parameterNotes) — named honestly rather than implied solved by PAR_FRY's addition.
metadata.invalidTransitionsAudit2026-08-16: Dedicated follow-up audit, the SAME rigor egg.json got on 2026-08-15 (invalidTransitionsNote above), triggered by src/reachability.ts (TICKET 4, PAPER_NOTES_2608.04768.md) finding — via pure graph search, not injected — that 'mashed potato -> goal peeled' was reachable through 'mashed -> fry -> peel', because NOTHING forbade PEEL on an already-fried potato. Checked individually, not batch-asserted (the exact discipline the ORIGINAL 2026-08-15 mistake skipped, per invalidTransitionsNote above): eight cut-shape states (sliced/diced/julienne/chopped/minced/halved/quartered/grated) now forbid 'peeled' at HIGH confidence — structural, direct mirror of egg.json's sliced/diced/chopped forbidding peeled: once subdivided into pieces, there is no single whole piece left to revert to 'peeled'. 'fried'/'baked'/'par_fried' also now forbid 'peeled', but at the SAME WEAKER 'no real counter-technique found on active search' tier egg.json's own fried/poached-forbidding-boiled entries use, not the structural tier — named as such, not presented with equal confidence. Deliberately does NOT touch 'boiled': boil-in-jacket-then-peel is the real, verified, common technique this repo already corrected itself over once (invalidTransitionsNote above) — the honest physical distinction is that BOILING is a gentle, WET process that doesn't fundamentally alter the skin the way FRYING/BAKING's dry/oil heat does, not an arbitrary inconsistency. Also deliberately does NOT add shape-to-shape closures (e.g. diced forbidding sliced) — real progressive-cutting techniques exist (halved -> quartered -> diced is a genuine real sequence) and this session did not have the confidence to individually verify which shape-to-shape transitions are and aren't real, so none were asserted rather than guessed; a real, named, still-open gap, not silently closed. Does NOT forbid cut-shape <-> cooked-state transitions in either direction (dicing a boiled potato for salad, boiling diced potato for hash — both real, common, unblocked, correctly) — CUT/GRATE's own statePrerequisites (washed/peeled) already gate re-cutting separately from this field. Proven via scripts/is-goal-still-reachable.ts (npm run capability-test:reachability) — 'mashed -> peeled' is now correctly unreachable via the fry route; see that script's own updated narration.
metadata.failureStateNote: 'burned'/'overcooked' added 2026-08-16 (TICKET 5, PAPER_NOTES_2608.04768.md): this engine could express every way a dish goes RIGHT and none of the ways it goes wrong. Deliberately NOT wired to any detection mechanism — no timer, no probability, no burn inference; that requires perception (ENGINE_INVARIANTS.md #11, out of scope here). Reachable today only as an AUTHORED starting/mid-recipe fact (RecipeInstanceSchema.state accepts any string) — e.g. a recipe modeling 'the robot discovers this potato is already burned, what can it still do' — the same honest scope as every other informational parameter in this vocabulary; a future perception layer is what would actually ASSERT this state, not this repo. 'burned' is fully terminal (invalidTransitions forbids every other state, including 'overcooked' — a real, structural fact: charred/carbonized potato has no rescue, matching this ticket's own framing that terminality 'is the point'). 'overcooked' forbids reverting/re-cooking into every NORMAL state (peeled/cut-shapes/boiled/fried/baked/mashed) — a deliberate SIMPLIFICATION, stated rather than hidden, not a claim every one of those transitions is definitively impossible: a genuinely mushy over-boiled potato mashing into something edible is real technique (the same rescue mashNote above already documents for a DIFFERENT starting point), but MASH's own statePrerequisites (['boiled','baked']) doesn't list 'overcooked' as an allowed starting state, so wiring that real rescue through for real would need touching statePrerequisites too — a small, genuine follow-up, deliberately not done here to keep this ticket's scope to reachable states and their closures, not new action wiring. Unlike 'burned', 'overcooked' does NOT forbid transitioning to 'burned' itself (a real, physically plausible further progression, even though nothing today drives it) — which means `isTerminalState(potato, "overcooked")` correctly computes `false`, not `true`: only 'burned' is unconditionally terminal here, 'overcooked' is terminal for RECOVERY purposes only, still able to degrade further. Checked by running the actual function, not just asserted — see scripts/failure-states-as-a-robot.ts's own output. Neither state blocks tag-only actions like SALT/PEPPER (engine.ts's applyAction only checks invalidTransitions against a COMPUTED STATE change, never against an addsTag-only action) — seasoning a burned potato is pointless but not schema-forbidden, the identical state-vs-tag distinction this schema already draws everywhere else, not a new gap.
metadata.drainedTagNote: isDrainable + DRAIN (data/actions/drain.json), added 2026-08-16, closes a real, previously-missing step: crispy-french-fries.json and salted-fried-potatoes.json both went straight from FRY to SALT with nothing removing the clinging surface oil first. See drain.json's own methodNote for the real, cited wire-rack-vs-paper-towel crispness difference. A tag, not a state, for the same orthogonal-fact reasoning as 'washed'/'broken' — a potato is still 'fried' after draining, just also now 'drained'.
metadata.brokenTagNote: 'broken' added 2026-08-16, directly answering a real user question about frying: constant stirring of already-softened potato pieces can mechanically fracture them, a genuinely different real failure from burned/overcooked — see fry.json's own agitationNote for the full cited mechanism (Binner et al. 2000, peer-reviewed pectin/cell-wall-softening science) and its honest 'this repo's own inference, not directly stated' caveat on the stirring-causes-breakage step specifically. A TAG, not a state, on purpose: unlike burned/overcooked (mutually-exclusive forms a piece either is or isn't), a piece can be simultaneously 'fried' AND 'broken' — breakage is an orthogonal structural fact about a piece's integrity, not a different cooking stage, the same state-vs-tag distinction 'washed' was moved across in this exact file. Same TICKET-5 discipline as burned/overcooked: reachable ONLY as an authored fact (no detection mechanism — FRY's agitation parameter is informational only, per action.ts's own no-conditional-output-per-parameter-value limitation, so nothing here derives 'broken' automatically from choosing constant_stir), not silently implied to be causally modeled. Not added to onion.json/garlic.json (also cut+fried) in this pass — a real, named, still-open extension, not silently assumed covered.
